title: Prove authenticated GitHub observation in Node Vitest

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage verdict: **Caught.** The maintained tests fail when the one-call-first rule after a wait is broken. Story SEED-413#authenticated-github-observation-via-vitest (slice 2 promise), revision fa4d5c57608966483d829faae8feba252e6c22c8.

Invocation start: 2026-11-27T22:40:33+08:00 (host clock). Report produced 58.8 s later (measured), at about 22:41:32+08:00.

**Promise checked:** "When the wait ends, one call goes first. Its new limit holds back the rest."

**Fault:** I used your second suggestion, letting every queued call go when the wait ends. The change was in `ReadAdmission#turnsOpen()` in `Distribution/src/skills/dough-execute-plan/scripts/github-request-admission.mjs` (edited in the scratch checkout only):
```
- return this.#resuming ? 1 : requestsUnderWayLimit;
+ return requestsUnderWayLimit;
```
I left fixtures and assertions unchanged. The other suggested fault (queued requests sent during a directed wait) was not probed. Its maintained owner looks like `authenticated-read-admission.spec.ts:125` together with the held-back check in `github-request-calls.mjs`.

**Runs** (fresh scratch worktree, deps from `node scripts/setup-native.mjs npm`, your focused command with `env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR` and `--workers=1`):

| Run | Result | Vitest duration |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 17/17 passed in 2 files, all ran, including resumption.spec.ts:65 on the real CLI path | 5.00 s |
| Fault applied | 7 failed, 10 passed | 2.71 s |
| Restored | 17/17 passed | 2.48 s |

**What caught it:**
- **End to end:** `authenticated-read-resumption.spec.ts:65` failed at `expect(github.calls).toHaveLength(2)`, which received 4. This is the independent check on the production path (execGh, the owner, the real gh CLI, then the fake GitHub). After the wait ended, all three queued reads reached GitHub instead of one going first.
- **Unit level:** `authenticated-read-admission.spec.ts:169` and `:184` (directed and backed-off cases) and `:211` (2 cases) failed at `expect(await settledOf(rest)).toEqual([false, false])`, receiving `[true, true]`. The rest got turns before the first read ended.
- The 10 tests that still passed don't depend on this rule.
- The claim covers the after-wait resumption path within one owner process.

**Restoration:** an EXIT trap ran `git checkout` on the file. `git status` and `git diff` were then empty, matching the clean starting state, and the restored run passed 17/17. I removed the scratch worktree with `git worktree remove` and confirmed it no longer appears in `git worktree list`. The execution worktree was not touched.

**Next proof action:** none needed for this promise. If you want the other half covered, probe queued requests being sent during a wait. No earlier disposition matched, and no repair decision follows from this probe.

**Costs:**
- **Test runtime:** measured from Vitest's duration figures, about 10.2 s across the three runs (5.00 + 2.71 + 2.48 s). This excludes npm startup. Machine load average was about 4.5.
- **Human effort:** unavailable; no human took part and there is no separate measure.
- **Agent effort:** unavailable; there is no separate token or tool-time measure.
- **Invocation-to-report elapsed:** 58819 ms, measured from 1795790433000 to 1795790491819 Unix epoch ms. This covers lookup, setup and all runs, and was sampled by `finish-report.mjs`.

Wrap-up disposition: fa4d5c57608966483d829faae8feba252e6c22c8, Caught, no follow-up.
